title: Fourier factors of a partite matching
statement: Let $q,k,n$ be nonnegative integers with $n>0$, let $f$ be any real-valued function on the Boolean cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$, and let $M$ be a perfect matching in the complete $q$-partite graph with $k$ vertices in each part. Assign independently and uniformly a label from $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ to each edge of $M$. For each part, form the set of labels on its incident matching edges, and let its factor be the absolute value of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ indexed by that set, where the Fourier coefficient at $S$ is the uniform average of $f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$. The expected product of the part factors is at most the product, over all parts, of the square root of the expected squared factor for that part.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
$M$ is a perfect matching in the complete $q$-partite graph with $k$ vertices per part
